sections.content:
Check the other reviews to see what topics are being taught. I am just going to write what I feel about the content here.
If you are not a math major, I would suggest you not to take this course when Maximilian is teaching. He came from 2431 so he takes a rigorous approach to teach probability. To understand what a rigorous approach of probability is, I will show you a simple concept of probability space in this course.

A probability space is a tuple of (Omega, F, P) which refers to the sample space, event space, and probability measure respectively.
The sample space is the collection of all possible outcomes of a random trial. e.g. {Head, Tail} for a coin flip, {1,2,3,4,5,6} for a dice roll.
The event space is a collection of subsets of the sample space. For example, {1,2,3}, {2,3,4} could be events in the event space. But there are certain restrictions you have to follow when defining an event space.
At last, the probability measure is a function mapping from every event to a number in the real number line from 0 to 1.

If you are struggling to understand or just have no interest in what I have mentioned above, you should wait until this guy is not teaching this course. Personally, I enjoyed it very well I think this is the only correct way to learn probability. But I do understand that not just math majors are taking this course and non-math majors wouldn't be interested to learn probability in such depth.

For math majors, I would suggest you to take this course. After taking this course, I just think this is the only correct way to learn probability. I enjoyed this course a lot and I think you are a math enthusiast, you would enjoy it as well.
A suggestion I would give to math majors is to take this course with math2033 as well. Foundation in analysis would really help in this course sometimes, and helps you think deeper to understand more of what's going on.

sections.content: The course content serves as a comprehensive introduction to the fundamental principles of probability theory. It systematically builds from the very basics, like sample spaces and combinatorics, to more advanced and fascinating concepts such as conditional probability, discrete and continuous random variables, and expectation. The latter part of the course, covering limit theorems like the Law of Large Numbers and the Central Limit Theorem, is particularly rewarding as it bridges theoretical probability with real-world statistical applications. As the description states, the mathematical prerequisites are quite manageable; a solid grasp of first-year calculus (especially integration for continuous distributions) is truly all you need to succeed. The material is challenging but logically structured, making it accessible for students who keep up with the weekly lectures and problem sets.
sections.teaching: The teaching quality is a major highlight of this course. The professor is exceptionally clear and well-organized. The prof will send handwrite notes and records on Canvas.
sections.grading: The grading scheme for this course is transparent and fair, typically comprising homework assignments, one or two midterm exams, and a comprehensive final.
sections.workload: The workload for MATH 2421 is moderate but requires consistent attention. You can expect a weekly problem set that takes a few hours to complete, depending on your familiarity with the topics. These assignments are not merely busywork; they are critical for cementing your understanding of the lecture material.

sections.teaching:
The instruction provided is insufficient in preparing students for what they will encounter. There is a lack of comprehensive examples to facilitate intuitive understanding of the content. The underlying motivations behind many concepts or distributions are not explained adequately. This approach does not align with effective teaching methods for a mathematics course.

Furthermore, the course content was not completed within the allocated timeframe. As a result, the instructor hastily covered the remaining material in a makeup lecture during the study period, which took place less than a week before the final exam.

The provided notes are also unhelpful. Unlike most professors who share complete notes, the instructor uploads condensed versions that lack useful examples, proofs, and other important details discussed in class. Moreover, these notes are not conducive to efficient revision as they consist of a disjointed mix of MS Word documents, screenshots of LaTeX papers, or even a PDF compilation of images for a single chapter.

- List of topcis

Chapter 1 : Preliminary
Chapter 2 : Probability
Chapter 3 : Random Variables and Probabilty Distributions
Chapter 4 : Joint and Conditional Probability Distributions
Chapter 5 : Covariance, Correlation, and Moment Generating Functions

- Brief comment on each chapter

> Ch1 is simply a revision of secondary school thing, n!, nCr, nPr, (a+b)^n = ..., etc
> Ch2 is basic probability, like the famous birthday problem. It is basic since it uses basic concept, not because it is easy!
> Ch3-4 is something real
1. Single-variable distribution
You will learn up to
   > 6 discrete distribution, and
   > 6 continuous distribution
You are required to learn the intuition, formula, properties (like memoryless), relationship between distribution, and distribution approximation.
2. Multivariable distribution
Besides these (1-dim) distribution, you will also learn joint distribution, like multinomial (discrete) and multi-normal (continuous)
3. Conditional distribution (single or multi-variable)
> Ch5 is something fun
It covers moment of generating function (mgf) and uniqueness of mgf per distribution
It generalizes the process like finding expectation, variance, or in general the expectation of a vector
It is hard and abstract, but prof didn't try to scare us by crazy stuff, what u learn is still the basic to this topic and, to be honest, quite fun

- Sum-up

so, main coverage:
1. Single-variable, Discrete and Continuous distribution
2. Joint distribution
3. Conditional distribution
4. Moments

But I want to point out that Chapter 4 and Chapter 5, the last two chapters are really hard and need to use more time to study and focus on. Chapter 4 is about the two random variables, the joint pmf,pdf and marginal pmt, pdf. Those kind of different combination things. You should have basic skills on multivariable calculus so as to understand and know how to integrate the functions.
sections.teaching: Professor used powerpoint and notes to teach the students. Normally, he uploads the notes to his webpage. You can find the notes and assignments there. I suggest you print out the notes since there are a lot of spaces that are empty, maybe the instructor wants the students join the lectures and write those things down by themselves. So, don't miss and lessons. Once I was sick I still got back to the school for his lesson.
sections.grading:
I don't think the grading is good. Since it is normal for students to do much better in the mid-term exam than the final exam.

In this semester, the mid-term exam just included basic probability and different distributions(Poisson, Binomial, Normal, Negative Binomial, Geometric). So, most of the students can do it well. As well as the instructor provided the formula sheet for the students and you can create your own cheat sheet at the same time, so this helped students need not to remember the distribution functions by themselves.

After the mid-term exam, as I said before, the main character will be the Two or More Random Variables. The general concepts are not difficult to understand but I think there are not enough examples to let students digest what is going on. I suggested you have to do the questions by yourself and check the solutions. Since those solutions have been provided.

As I heard that, staying at mean can get a B-/C+. Fewer students get B-, much more students get a C+. So, I don't think the grading is good.
sections.workload: I think not really hard, only 3 assignments need to be handed in. But some of the questions you can find out in the notes or past paper. So, I think one to two hours will be enough for an assignment. And usually, the instructor released the homework a month before the deadline, I believe the time should be enough for you to do it.

sections.content:
这门课的主要内容:
midterm前 (discrete):
- permutations，combinations
- inclusion-exclusion
- multinomial theorem
- conditional probability
- independence of RV
- law of total probability
- baye’s theorem
- PDF, CDF, expectation, variance
- discrete distributions（bernoulli，binomial，poisson，geometric，negative binomial）

midterm后 (discrete + continuous):
- discrete distributions（hypergeometric，multinomial）
- continuous distributions（normal [multivariate] + normal approximation，gamma，exponential，beta，uniform，log-normal）
- distribution of function of continuous RV
- joint PDF，CDF
- conditional PDF，CDF and conditional expectation
- independence of RV (in terms of PDF)
- skewness and kurtosis
- distribution of real／vector valued function or RV
- central limit theorem
- covariance，correlation, variance of sum of RV
- moment generating function （核心部分）

乍看之下，这门课的内容有很多，但其实midterm前有很多内容是在其它课上过了的（例如COMP 2711，MATH 2343，MATH 2411），因此对于CS的童鞋，有些内容可能会学3遍。不同的是，作为统计学／概率学第一门教得比较深入的课（我不会把MATH 2411归类为统计学课，它只是一门教公式＋计算的课），从discrete到continuous到moment generating function，这门课更着重于证明（虽然有时并不太严谨），也让我对概率学有了更全面的认知。因此，强烈建议CS的童鞋们直接waive掉MATH 2411去上这门课。

教授的笔记有很多部分都是要填空的，所以建议童鞋们去上课。还有教授有时会给一些能得bonus分的in-class question，所以不上课的话就无法得到了。

希望这门课的教授会跟MATH 2411和COMP 2711的教授讨论和重整这三门课的内容，因为实在有不少重叠之处。这样就能分配更多时间到midterm后的核心内容。

sections.teaching: Errrr```This professor has terrible accent...I cannot hear him clearly, nor can I focus at all. He did not explain the examples enough, just read it, not leading us through the thinking process. So mostly it is just a self-taught course then.
sections.grading: 2 quiz, 1 midterm, 1 final. attendance enough to get 2% extra. the quiz and exam are standard.
sections.workload:
4 sets of homework no need to hand in.
It has 'questions not from textbook' and 'questions from textbook' part. Some of those not from textbook are quite difficult but you can try to do it on your own, for your benefit. Exam most likely those 'from textbook'. But no need to buy or read the textbook.

sections.content: Rich (in proofs). Easy in the beginning. Notes are sufficient but have too many fill in the blanks. So while you're blindly copying from the board, you're wasting precious hours. If you miss the lectures you may not only have to google the difficult-to-find answers, but may also miss the in-class assignments (2% each) which should be outlawed from grading since the answer is given in the classroom (basically surprise attendance).
sections.teaching: The prof is a good person, for he easily increases your score during paper checking and sympathizes with your unfortunately humongous schedule. However, his teaching is lackluster, dispirited (since he is prone to mumbling to an audience) and limited to writing on the whiteboard that which could have simply been filled into the notes. But you don't have an option to take another prof as long as you take this course in spring.
sections.grading:
Since there is no homework enforced, if you lack the motivation to practice yourself, your grades will plummet. Naturally! But if you practice, it pays.

The mean is around 50-60% (C range)
SD is around 20
sections.workload: Extensive and heavy, only if you have never done it before and have to do it yourself. And practice proofs and derivations more than anything else. By the end, you'll realize how easy a course this was if only it had been taught better. So yea, the workload really depends on your level of logical understanding.

sections.content: The teaching material for this course is mainly about characteristics of different continuous or discrete distribution. Personally, I think it is relatively easy comparing to Multivariable Calculus. All you need to do is just understanding the proof shown in the lectures. And If you like statistic, this course will definitely make you very excited. But if you dislike statistic, then I recommend you not to take this course.
sections.teaching: His teaching approach is just reading out the lecture notes and writing some important equations for at least 1/3 of the lesson. However, those notes you have written down help you to remember the proof and logic, which are beneficial to your exam. As the other commentary said, checking paper is a good way for you to have a higher mark. Try to write steps for every questions since those steps are the key for a sub-grade.
sections.grading: His grade is comparatively better than other maths professor. For me, I would say his grading is fair. This Professor seems quite hard to get a A+.
sections.workload: He used in-class assignment as a way to take attendance. But you can use his lecture notes to deduce when will he approximately give out in class assignment. As I said, try not to skip any lectures. Apart from assignment, this course only needs mid term and final. You can skip mid-term if you think you are confident about your ability.
